partially_covered.missing: Organization attributes remain limited to name, GLN, and address; no additional details such as contact info, legal status, or other identifiers.

ValidationConstraint class exists, but there is still no explicit modeling of D96A mandatory fields or property-level cardinality restrictions. No SHACL shapes or OWL restrictions to enforce required fields.

cq_coverage.details: Coverage remains strong for most CQs, with only CQ5 (organization attribute detail) and CQ13 (explicit validation/must-have fields) still only partially addressed. No new CQs have become uncovered.

issues: Section subclasses (HeaderSection, DetailSection, SummarySection) are still defined as subclasses of InvoiceMessage, which is an inheritance misuse (composition should be via hasSection property only).

strengths: Deep class hierarchy reflecting EDIFACT structure
Consistent use of pivot classes and reification
Well-defined property characteristics and disjointness axioms
weaknesses: No General Class Axioms (GCAs) for advanced semantic inference
Composition vs. inheritance error in Section modeling
Validation and mandatory fields not formally encoded

likely_oops_pitfalls: P4: Missing domain or range for some inverse properties (minor, but most are present)
P7: Subclass misuse for composition (Section < InvoiceMessage)
reasoner_risks: Hermit/Pellet may warn about excessive use of AsymmetricProperty (not harmful, but unnecessary in some cases)
No illegal OWL 2 datatypes detected; all are compliant

suggestions_ignored: Expand Organization modeling to include all relevant attributes (CQ5)
Model mandatory D96A fields and validation requirements explicitly (CQ13)
Replace Section subclasses of InvoiceMessage with compositional object properties (composition vs. inheritance)
Introduce General Class Axioms (GCAs) for advanced reasoning
Add more detailed modeling for temporal aspects
improvement_tracking.notes: No substantive changes since the previous review; all major improvement suggestions remain unaddressed. The ontology maintains its previous quality and coverage, but does not show progress on known issues.

improvement_suggestions.suggestion: Expand Organization modeling to enumerate all relevant attributes (contact info, legal status, additional identifiers, etc.) to fully answer CQ5.
improvement_suggestions.expected_impact: Enables richer queries about organizations and improves CQ5 coverage.

improvement_suggestions.suggestion: Explicitly model D96A mandatory fields and validation requirements using OWL cardinality restrictions and/or SHACL shapes. For example, make hasReferenceNumber and hasDocumentDate mandatory for HeaderSection, and require at least one BuyerRole per InvoiceMessage.
improvement_suggestions.expected_impact: Enables automated validation and ensures file format validity for CQ13.

improvement_suggestions.suggestion: Correct the Section modeling: remove Section subclasses from InvoiceMessage inheritance hierarchy, and use only the hasSection object property for composition.
improvement_suggestions.expected_impact: Cleaner ontology structure, fewer validator warnings, and improved semantic clarity.

improvement_suggestions.suggestion: Introduce General Class Axioms (GCAs) to define, for example, BuyerOrganization as an Organization with at least one BuyerRole assignment.
improvement_suggestions.expected_impact: Enables more powerful reasoning and querying about organizational roles.

improvement_suggestions.suggestion: Add temporal modeling (e.g., transaction timestamps, validity periods) to support advanced business process queries.
improvement_suggestions.expected_impact: Improves ability to answer time-related queries and supports business process analytics.

summary: The ontology continues to provide strong structural coverage of EDIFACT invoice data, with deep hierarchies, robust annotations, and correct use of pivot classes. However, none of the previous review's high- or medium-priority improvement suggestions have been implemented. Quality and coverage remain stable but have not improved, and key issues such as composition vs. inheritance and explicit modeling of mandatory fields persist. Further refinement is needed to achieve full CQ coverage and optimal OWL 2 modeling practices.
